question.text: A sample of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>NaClO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> is converted by heat to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>NaCl</mi></math> with a loss of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>16</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of oxygen. The residue is dissolved in water and precipitated as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AgCl</mi></math>. The mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AgCl</mi></math> (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>) obtained will be: (Given: Molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AgCl</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>143</mn><mo>.5</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
2NaClO3→∆2NaCl+3O2
2 moles of NaCl=3 moles of oxygen
nNaCl=0.1632×23=1200×23=1300
The number of moles of NaCl=The number of moles of AgCl
1300=nAgCl
Weight of AgCl=1300×108+35.5=1300×143.5
=0.48 g
